How the Internet Works

1. Undersea Submarine Cables

Over 99% of international data travels through fiber-optic subsea cables laid on ocean floors. Pulsing laser light pulses carry terabits per second between continents!

2. TCP 3-Way Handshake

Before downloading a webpage, your computer performs a handshake: SYN (Synchronize) ➔ SYN-ACK ➔ ACK (Acknowledge) to create a reliable connection.

3. Packet MTU & Fragmentation

Internet routers cannot pass infinitely large files. The Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) is usually 1500 Bytes. Large images/files get sliced into fragments and reassembled at destination!

4. Time To Live (TTL)

Every packet header includes a TTL counter (e.g., 64). Every router hop decrements TTL by 1. If TTL hits 0, the packet is discarded to prevent infinite routing loops!
